definitions.name: x2611_10667_p
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_10667_p (B C : ℕ) (t : ℚ) : Polynomial ℚ :=
  (-Polynomial.X) ^ B * Finset.sum (Finset.range (C + 2)) (fun i =>
    Polynomial.C ((1 - t) ^ ((C : ℤ) - (i : ℤ)) *
      (-t) ^ ((i : ℤ) - 1) *
      ((if i = 0 then 0 else (Nat.choose C (i - 1) : ℚ)) -
        t * (Nat.choose (C + 1) i : ℚ))) * Polynomial.X ^ i)
definitions.notes: The x-axis part of the polynomial P in (10), so the full polynomial is y^(qr)+p(x). Integer powers preserve the printed factors at the endpoints. The binomial coefficient with lower index −1 is interpreted as 0; ordinary binomial coefficients use Nat.choose. B,C are the positive representatives used in Section 3.

definitions.name: x2611_10667_torus_regular
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_10667_torus_regular {K : Type*} [Field K]
    (P : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K) : Prop :=
  ∀ z : Fin 2 → AlgebraicClosure K,
    (∀ i, z i ≠ 0) →
    MvPolynomial.eval₂ (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)) z P = 0 →
    ∃ i, MvPolynomial.eval₂ (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)) z
      (MvPolynomial.pderiv i P) ≠ 0
definitions.notes: Geometric nonsingularity of a bivariate hypersurface on the multiplicative torus: at every zero over the algebraic closure with both coordinates nonzero, at least one partial derivative is nonzero. This is the Jacobian criterion for smoothness of the displayed hypersurfaces, used to express face Δ_v-regularity.

statements.label: Claim 2 (the two displayed face reductions)
statements.name: x2611_10667_claim2
statements.original:
Claim 2: The two faces $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}$ are
 $\Delta_{v}$ -regular.

Proof of Claim 2. By Definition 2.2, we have

 ${P|_{F_{1}}}=y^{qr}+(-x)^{B}\sum_{i=0}^{C}(1-t)^{C-i}(-t)^{i-1}\left(\binom{C}{i-1}-t\binom{C+1}{i}\right)x^{i}$ 

and

 $P|_{F_{2}}=t^{C-1}(C-t(C+1))x^{qr}-t^{C}x^{qr+1}+y^{qr}.$ 

Let $u\equiv\frac{1-t}{\pi^{k}}\pmod{{\mathfrak{r}}}$ . Then the reduction $\overline{P|_{F_{1}}}$ equals

 $\overline{P|_{F_{1}}}=y^{qr}+u^{C}(-1)^{B}x^{B}\sum_{i=0}^{C}\binom{C}{i}(-x/u)^{i}=y^{qr}+(-x)^{B}(u-x)^{C},$ 

which defines a smooth curve in the $\mathbb{G}_{m}^{2}$ , where $\mathbb{G}_{m}$ stands for the multiplicative group.
A similar computation, using the fact that $C\equiv 1\pmod{r}$ , proves the result for $F_{2}$ .
